sources.entry: Polka - Turns the MacBook notch into a control center for VPN connections, tab groups from any browser, now playing, calendar, an on-device translator and clipboard history. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/romabmstu/polka) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Polka
summary.one_liner: Polka is a free, open-source macOS control center that lives in the MacBook notch (or menu bar on non-notch displays), offering browser tab groups, VPN toggles, now-playing controls, calendar, calculator, clipboard history and a file shelf.
use_cases: Switch system or Tunnelblick VPN connections from the notch
Save and organize browser tabs into nested groups
Control music playing in Spotify, Apple Music or a browser
Join the next Zoom, Meet, Teams or Telemost call in one click
Recover recently copied text, screenshots and images
Stage files temporarily and drag them into other apps or send via AirDrop
summary.what_it_does: Polka expands from the MacBook notch on hover or with the ⌥⇧K shortcut; on displays without a notch it becomes a compact menu bar control that follows the pointer between screens. It saves the current tab or window (⌥⇧S) or pasted links into nested, reorderable groups. It controls system VPNs and Tunnelblick, with FSNT / Throne requiring a local API setup. It shows artwork, progress and controls for the currently playing media app, shows a week view and agenda with one-click meeting joins, and includes a calculator that converts currencies. It also keeps a clipboard history of the last 30 items and a file shelf that stores references only, plus one-click "Focus" and "Call" presets.
notable: Open source, with code publicly viewable and builds published via GitHub Actions with provenance attestation on tagged releases
Lives in the MacBook notch, with menu bar fallback on non-notch displays
Clipboard history skips content marked as concealed/transient
caveats: Not yet notarized by Apple, so the first launch of a downloaded copy requires running an xattr command in Terminal
Clipboard history may still record unmarked passwords
Multiple VPNs can conflict over routes and DNS
